issue.title: library: Reasonix Studio gets no MCP servers, skills or hooks
issue.body:
## What

Reasonix Studio 2.x is wired as an Agent (model, planner, effort) but is missing from the
**Library** subsystem: magpie can't give it MCP servers, skills or hooks, and it isn't in the
project-skills table. Every neighbouring agent that shares the same kind of TOML config
(Kimi Code, Grok Build, DeepSeek Harness) has all four.

Tested on magpie 0.1.1352 with Studio 2.49.0 on Windows 11 (`%APPDATA%\reasonix\config.toml`).

## Reproduction

```console
$ magpie library mcp add probe https://example.com/mcp agents=reasonix
magpie: Reasonix Studio has no user-wide place for MCP servers that magpie knows of
  agents here that take MCP servers: claude, codex, opencode, mimocode, dsh, commandcode, qoder, qoder-cn, zcode, workbuddy

$ magpie library skill agents check reasonix
magpie: Reasonix Studio has no user-wide place for skills that magpie knows of
  agents here that take skills: claude, codex, opencode, mimocode, dsh, commandcode, qoder, qoder-cn, zcode, workbuddy
```

`magpie library` lists Reasonix Studio nowhere, while `magpie agents` shows it wired
(`executor magpie/qoder-cn/dfmodel · effort high`). The config file was unchanged by the run.

## Why it isn't wired

`internal/library/targets.go` has one `case "reasonix":` that sets `Instructions` only — no
`MCP`, no `Skills`:

```go
case "reasonix":
	// Reasonix reads every one there is of REASONIX.md, AGENTS.md and
	// CLAUDE.md in its state folder; REASONIX.md is its own
	t.Instructions = filepath.Join(reasonixState(a), "REASONIX.md")
```

`projectSkillsDirs` (`internal/library/projects.go`) has no `reasonix` entry, and `hookSpecOf`
has no `reasonix` case, so the page greyed its hook chip.

## Where Reasonix actually keeps them

Read from esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix (`internal/contract/config/`, `internal/ext/skill/`):

| Thing | Where | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP servers | `[[plugins]]` in the same `config.toml` magpie already edits | `name`, `type` = `stdio` (default) / `http` / `sse`, `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `headers`, `disabled_tools` |
| Skills (global) | `<reasonix home>/skills` | `%APPDATA%\reasonix\skills` on Windows; `$REASONIX_HOME/skills` when set |
| Skills (shared) | `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.agent/skills`, `~/.claude/skills` | `ConventionDirs = {".reasonix", ".agents", ".agent", ".claude"}`; `.reasonix` wins on a name clash |
| Skills (project) | `<workspace>/{.reasonix,.agents,.agent,.claude}/skills` | same convention list |
| Hooks | `.reasonix/settings.json` | not scanned across the convention dirs, so a separate file from `config.toml` |

`[[plugins]]` already mirrors Claude Code's `mcpServers` — `PluginEntry` in
`internal/contract/config/plugin_entry.go` says so in its doc comment — and Reasonix merges
`[[plugins]]` across `config.toml`, `reasonix.toml` and a project `.mcp.json` by name.

## What I'd expect

1. `t.MCP = &mcpFile{Path: a.Path, Format: fmtReasonix}` writing `[[plugins]]` in the same
   `config.toml` — the shape `fmtGrok` uses for `[mcp_servers.<name>]`, with
   `name`/`type`/`command`/`args`/`env`/`url`/`headers`.
2. `t.Skills = filepath.Join(a.Dir, "skills")` (the home magpie already resolves via
   `$REASONIX_HOME` / `%APPDATA%\reasonix`), and `SkillsAlso: []string{"agents"}`-style
   reading of the shared root, since Reasonix discovers `~/.agents/skills` on its own.
3. A `"reasonix"` entry in `projectSkillsDirs`.
4. A `hookSpecOf` case for `.reasonix/settings.json`, or an explicit "no hooks yet" reason if
   that file's hook schema isn't worth supporting.

Nothing here touches the model/planner/effort wiring from #427, which works.

## Notes

- Studio and the native CLI share these files, so #427's caveat applies: a running Studio picks
  up a new `[[plugins]]` on reload, not mid-turn.
- I only have Windows + Studio 2.49.0 here, so the macOS/Linux paths are unchecked; the state
  root is `$REASONIX_STATE_HOME` → `[storage] state` → the Reasonix home, which
  `reasonixState()` already resolves for the instructions file.

comments.body:
Wired — Reasonix Studio now takes the Library's MCP servers and skills. Branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/issue-batch-1024pm (commit [fd4bcb54](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/fd4bcb54), on current main dd1e8822).

- **MCP**: `[[plugins]]` in the same config.toml magpie already writes its provider into (new `fmtReasonix`). An entry is written as Reasonix's own config reads it: `name`, `type` stdio — which it takes as the default, said anyway — with `command`/`args`/`env`, or `http`/`sse` with a `url`; `disabled_tools` is its tools-off key. Writes go through the same array-table editor the provider itself uses (`SetTOMLArrayTable`), so the user's own `[[plugins]]`, `[[providers]]` and every other field of the file stay; read-back, discovery of the user's own plugins, and removal are tested, including a user plugin of each shape.
- **Skills**: `<reasonix home>/skills`, with `~/.claude/skills` read beside it (`SkillsAlso`, ConventionDirs); in a project `.reasonix/skills`, the shared `.agents/skills` beside that.
- **A server carrying `${references}` is refused** rather than guessed at — nothing documents Reasonix expanding any.

**Hooks stay unwired, deliberately**: where Reasonix keeps them (`.reasonix/settings.json`) is known, but the names of its hook events are not — wiring a guessed schema would write files it may not read. If you can point at where its events are named in esengine/DeepSeek-Reasonix (`hookSpecOf` takes one more case), hooks can follow the same pattern.

Verified: `go test ./internal/library -count=1` (410 tests, green; the new test red on main: no MCP target for reasonix). Not tested here: a real Windows install — the `%APPDATA%` path is exercised through sandboxed home variables only, as your report documented it.

Thanks — I read `fd4bcb54` and the MCP side looks right to me (`[[plugins]]` in the same `config.toml`, `SetTOMLArrayTable` so the user's own array tables survive, `disabled_tools` as the tools-off key).

Everything below is checked against **Studio 2.50.0** (`studio-v2.50.0`, tag `7bca7b7c`), which is the build on this machine, not the native CLI.

## Hooks: the event names are Claude Code's, verbatim

You were right not to guess, but the schema is in the source. `internal/ext/hook/hook.go` declares the events as exact strings:

```go
PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest,
UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure, PostLLMCall,
SessionStart, SessionEnd, SubagentStart, SubagentStop,
Notification, PreCompact
```

That is Claude Code's own list, and the comment in `internal/contract/config/paths.go` says the split is deliberate:

> hooks are NOT scanned across these — a `.claude/settings.json` uses a different hook schema that can't be parsed as ours, so hooks stay in `.reasonix/settings.json`

So the file is right, the event keys are the names magpie already writes for Claude Code, and only the entry shape differs:

| | Claude Code `settings.json` | Reasonix `settings.json` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field | `matcher` | **`match`** (anchored regex: `file` does *not* match `read_file`) |
| field | `command` (ignored; `hooks` is a nested array) | **`command`**, the thing that runs |
| nesting | `hooks.<Event>[].hooks[]` | `hooks.<Event>[]` directly |

Per-entry optional fields Reasonix honours: `description`, `timeout` (**milliseconds**, overriding the per-event default), `cwd`, `env`.

Two caveats before wiring it:

1. **`match` is an anchored regex, not a glob with pipes.** `Edit|Write|MultiEdit` happens to be a valid regex so it carries over, but a `Bash(go test:*)`-style permission string is not a matcher and would be an invalid regex. `ValidateMatcher` rejects it, so it fails loudly rather than silently — good — but a portable `tools: {shell: ..., edit: ...}` table needs regex-shaped values.
2. **`timeout` is milliseconds.** Magpie already writes Gemini CLI timeouts in ms, so there's precedent, but it's the opposite of the seconds-shaped fields elsewhere in `hookSpec`.

On this machine `%APPDATA%\reasonix\settings.json` already exists holding `{"hooks": {}}`, written by Reasonix itself, so the file is there to append to.

## Skills: `~/.agents/skills` needs the `readsShared` list, not `SkillsAlso`

`targets.go` currently has:

```go
t.Skills = filepath.Join(a.Dir, "skills")
t.SkillsAlso = []string{"claude"}
```

I want to correct something I nearly got wrong, because the two mechanisms look interchangeable and are not:

- `SkillsAlso` holds **agent IDs**, not paths — `targets.go` compares with `o.Agent.ID`, and `wslTargetOf` rewrites them to `id@distro`. So `"claude"` means Claude Code's own folder, `~/.claude/skills`. Adding `"codex"` would mean `~/.codex/skills` — **not** the shared root that Reasonix actually reads.
- `~/.agents/skills` is expressed by `readsShared` in `targets.go` (the same list Kimi Code, Goose, Cindy, Grok Build and friends are on). That flag is what lets `syncSkills` skip a duplicate link when a skill is already in the shared folder, and what makes `sync.go` report the skill as `Always` for the agent.

Meanwhile Studio 2.50.0's `internal/ext/skill/skill.go` walks `ConventionDirs` = `{".reasonix", ".agents", ".agent", ".claude"}` under `$HOME` unconditionally:

```go
if config.IsolatedHomeDir() == "" {
    for _, c := range config.ConventionDirs {
        dirs = append(dirs, de{filepath.Join(s.homeDir, c, SkillsDirname), ScopeGlobal, ...})
    }
}
```

So as things stand, a skill the user keeps in `~/.agents/skills` is loaded by Reasonix at runtime but invisible to the Library's accounting for it — "which agents have this skill" would leave Reasonix out while it reads the folder. On this machine that is 10 skills under `~/.agents/skills` beside 22 under `%APPDATA%\reasonix\skills`.

Suggested fix: add `"reasonix"` to `readsShared`. `.agent` can stay uncovered — no magpie target uses it either.

The same is true one level down: `projectSkillsDirs["reasonix"] = ".reasonix/skills"` covers one of the four convention dirs a project gets. That may be deliberate (magpie's project table also lists a single dir per agent), so I'd only flag it, not ask for it.

## Verification offer

I have Studio 2.50.0 and magpie 0.1.1364 here on Windows, and `%APPDATA%\reasonix\` is a real install rather than a sandbox. Say which commit to build and I'll run the Library sync against it and report what it writes.

@FuchaZ Thanks for the Studio 2.50.0 source pointers and for offering a real Windows check. I have implemented the remaining Reasonix Library integration directly, in a **standalone branch** rather than the mixed round-10 batch:

https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/reasonix-library-complete-1024
head: `cf87dc37c09e5b6fbadebfd7ebc8adcd9f102290`

This branch is based on upstream `dd1e8822` and contains the #3401 MCP/skills baseline plus:
- Hooks in Reasonix's **own** `<Reasonix home>/settings.json`, `hooks.<Event>[]` flat entries (not Claude's nested form).
- Portable and Reasonix-native event names from `internal/ext/hook/hook.go`. Tool matchers use anchored regex against the actual native tool names (`bash`, `edit_file`, `write_file`, `multi_edit`); `timeout` is stored in **milliseconds**.
- Skill accounting for `~/.agents/skills` via `readsShared`, in addition to Reasonix's own and Claude's skill folders.
- Round-trip and ownership checks: write, read, remove only Magpie-managed entries, preserve the user's existing hooks, settings and MCP array tables.

`go test -tags nogui ./internal/library -count=1` passes on this branch; Linux and Windows/amd64 static vet passed. **I have not run Reasonix natively on Windows**, so please do not treat this as a native end-to-end check.

If you can build this exact head against your Reasonix Studio 2.50.0 installation, please verify that Library-created hooks actually fire for `bash` and `edit_file/write_file`, that existing `settings.json` entries remain untouched when a Library hook is removed, and that shared skills under `~/.agents/skills` are correctly reported. A redacted before/after config and the first event's result would be valuable. Thanks again for the precise schema details.

This is a fork contribution offered for review, not a claim that upstream has accepted it.

comments.body:
Ran it. Built `cf87dc37` with Go 1.26.8 (portable, nothing installed) and exercised it against a **real Windows install**, not a sandbox: Reasonix Studio **2.50.0** (`reasonix-studio-electron`, read from `resources/app.asar`) with magpie 0.1.1391 on Windows 11. All three things you asked for are below.

## 1. Library-created hooks do fire, for `bash`

Wrote a `UserPromptSubmit` hook through `magpie library sync`, then drove a turn with the Studio CLI's own non-interactive mode (`reasonix -p --permission-mode danger-full-access`). The hook ran:

```
PRE  2026/10/24 23:03:09.28
POST 2026/10/24 23:03:09.54
```

Those two lines are the `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` probes I had in `settings.json` firing around an actual `bash` call in the turn, so `match: "^(bash|edit_file|write_file|multi_edit)$"` matches the **native** Reasonix tool name, exactly as you wrote it. The turn itself ran `echo HOOK_E2E_TEST_12345` and returned it.

One thing worth recording for upstream: Studio reports the file as loaded, so you can check a machine without running a turn.

```
$ reasonix hook list --json
{"hooks":[{"event":"PostToolUse","match":"^(bash|edit_file|write_file|multi_edit)$","scope":"global","status":"active"},
          {"event":"PreToolUse","match":"^(bash|edit_file|write_file|multi_edit)$","scope":"global","status":"active"}]}
```

## 2. Existing entries survive, in both directions

Put a user-owned entry in the file first:

```json
"Stop": [{ "command": "...", "description": "USER-OWNED-HOOK" }]
```

Then `magpie library sync` with a Library hook ticked for reasonix. Both ended up in the file, the user's untouched:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "UserPromptSubmit": [ { "command": "..." } ],   <- magpie's
    "PreToolUse":  [ { "match": "...", "command": "..." } ],
    "PostToolUse": [ { "match": "...", "command": "..." } ],
    "Stop": [ { "command": "...", "description": "USER-OWNED-HOOK" } ]   <- the user's, verbatim
  }
}
```

Then removed the Library hook and synced again. `UserPromptSubmit` went, `Stop` stayed byte-identical, with its `description` intact.

Same for MCP, on the array-table side: added a server with `library mcp add … agents=reasonix`, confirmed `name = 'probe-x'` landed in `config.toml` beside the user's own six `[[plugins]]`, removed it, and the six were unchanged and the probe gone. `[[providers]]` and the rest of the file were never touched.

## 3. `~/.agents/skills` accounting

`reasonix` is in `readsShared`, and `TestReasonixSharedSkillsAccounting` passes here — a skill present in `~/.agents/skills` is now reported as one reasonix has, instead of silently being read at runtime while the Library says it doesn't have it.

Your own test file covers it; I did not construct a separate end-to-end fixture for this one, since the unit test asserts exactly the `Always` membership the page reads.

## Test evidence

```
$ go test -tags nogui ./internal/library -run 'Reasonix' -count=1 -v
--- PASS: TestReasonixHooksOwnShapeAndPreservation (0.08s)
--- PASS: TestReasonixSharedSkillsAccounting (0.04s)
--- PASS: TestReasonixPluginsMCP (0.06s)
PASS
ok  github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/library  0.270s
```

**Caveats, stated plainly:**

- I exercised hooks through the **Studio CLI** (`reasonix -p`), which shares `<Reasonix home>/settings.json` with the desktop app but is not the Electron window. Same loader, same file, same 2.50.0 build — but if you want the GUI path specifically, that is still untested.
- My probe hooks were removed and both files restored to their exact prior contents afterwards; `settings.json` is back to `{"hooks": {}}` and `config.toml` still has its original six `[[plugins]]`. No before/after diff of a *user-owned* MCP or hook is included because I would rather not publish your config — the shape above is the redacted version.
- Everything ran on this machine's real `%APPDATA%\reasonix`, with magpie's own backups taken at each sync (`~/.config/magpie/backups/…`), so each step is reversible.

Two small observations while I was in there, neither blocking:

- `library sync` reports `✓ written into reasonix` even when only hooks changed, which reads a little oddly when the log above it says MCP servers were untouched.
- The hook row's `match` is stored as `^(bash|edit_file|write_file|multi_edit)$`. Reasonix anchors it again itself (`^(?:` + m + `)$`), so it's harmless, but `^…$` in the stored value double-anchors.

Nice work on the flat `match`/`command`/`timeout` shape — it lines up with the 2.50.0 source exactly, and the round-trip preserved the user's entry with its `description` intact without any special-casing.

这份验证已记录在案，round-13 留的"真实 Windows Studio 2.50.0 上验证 hook 触发与共享技能识别"这一项就此关闭：`PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` 探针在真实 `bash` 调用前后触发（原生工具名匹配生效）、用户自有的 `Stop` 条目与六个 `[[plugins]]` 在双向同步后逐字节保留、`~/.agents/skills` 经 `readsShared` 计入。`hook list --json` 能离线确认装载，这条对上游也有用，记下了。GUI（Electron 窗口）路径仍未测，与你的 caveat 一致——CLI 与桌面共用同一 loader 和 settings.json，风险很小，但不算已验证。

两个观察都收到，都同意不阻塞，说明一下我们的取舍：

- **match 双重锚定**：同意是无操作——Reasonix 包一层 `^(?:…)$` 后，`^(?:^X$)$` 与 `^X$` 匹配的串完全相同。锚定形态是 magpie 的规范条目形状：同步记录按它做认领与移除（`internal/library/hooks.go` 的 records 比对），且正是这份在真机上验证过触发行为的形状。改成不锚定需要重新走一遍真机验证才能声称有效，收益只是文件里少四个字符，所以暂时保留；如果上游愿意收，随收随改。
- **"✓ written into reasonix"**：`Changed` 的语义是"哪些 agent 的文件被写过"，即使只动了 hooks 一节，settings.json 确实重写了。让它按节报变化需要重构 Result 的粒度，为此一项只影响观感的输出不值得，保留原样。

两处都已记入本 fork 的 ledger 与 evidence（[comment 6385801640](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3401#issuecomment-6385801640)，你的测试输出与保留意见一并）。你环境里probe 的清理与备份说明也已记录。

## 摘要（给扫 issue 的人看）

**问题**：Reasonix Studio 在 magpie 里只接了模型（executor/planner/effort），Library 层的 MCP、skills、hooks 全都没有。结果是：在 Library 页面里配好 MCP 和技能，勾选不到 Reasonix Studio。

**现状**：**实现已经写好了，只差维护者收割。**

- 代码：`skygunner/magpie` 分支 `fix/reasonix-library-complete-1024`，head `cf87dc37`
- 覆盖：MCP（`[[plugins]]`）、skills（含 `~/.agents/skills`）、hooks（`.reasonix/settings.json`）三项齐全
- 验证：**已在真实 Windows 上跑通** —— Reasonix Studio 2.50.0 + magpie 0.1.1391，`PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` 在真实 `bash` 调用前后触发，用户自有 hook 与 6 个 `[[plugins]]` 双向同步逐字节保留

以上细节都在本 issue 前面的评论里（含 Studio 源码里的 hooks schema、字段差异、真机测试输出）。

**不需要再讨论设计了，只差有人把它并进 main。** 这个仓库现在不收外部 PR，所以只能等维护者看到这条。

---

## 中文补充：为什么我在意这个

我用 Reasonix Studio（2.50.0）作为主力 agent，同时也用 magpie 统一管理模型。

现在的情况有点尴尬：

- 模型能选 magpie 的 ✅
- 但 Library 里配的 MCP、技能、hooks 给不了它 ❌

更麻烦的是它**看起来像能用**：Studio 里确实能看到 context7、deepwiki 这些 MCP，但那是 Reasonix 自己去读 `~/.claude.json` 蹭来的，不是 magpie 配的。所以在 magpie 里「按 Agent 启用 MCP」这个动作，对它完全无效——勾不上，也没提示为什么。

期待的行为很简单：

| 功能 | 期望 |
| --- | --- |
| MCP 服务器 | 能勾选 Reasonix Studio，写进 `config.toml` 的 `[[plugins]]` |
| Skills | 能勾选，写进 `<reasonix home>/skills`，并识别 `~/.agents/skills` |
| Hooks | 能勾选，写进 `.reasonix/settings.json` |

不用改模型那条链路，那部分（#427）一直好好的。

感谢。


I want to correct something I nearly got wrong, because the two mechanisms look interchangeable and are not:

- `SkillsAlso` holds **agent IDs**, not paths — `targets.go` compares with `o.Agent.ID`, and `wslTargetOf` rewrites them to `id@distro`. So `"claude"` means Claude Code's own folder, `~/.claude/skills`. Adding `"codex"` would mean `~/.codex/skills` — **not** the shared root that Reasonix actually reads.
- `~/.agents/skills` is expressed by `readsShared` in `targets.go` (the same list Kimi Code, Goose, Cindy, Grok Build and friends are on). That flag is what lets `syncSkills` skip a duplicate link when a skill is already in the shared folder, and what makes `sync.go` report the skill as `Always` for the agent.

Meanwhile Studio 2.50.0's `internal/ext/skill/skill.go` walks `ConventionDirs` = `{".reasonix", ".agents", ".agent", ".claude"}` under `$HOME` unconditionally:

```go
if config.IsolatedHomeDir() == "" {
    for _, c := range config.ConventionDirs {
        dirs = append(dirs, de{filepath.Join(s.homeDir, c, SkillsDirname), ScopeGlobal, ...})
    }
}
```

So as things stand, a skill the user keeps in `~/.agents/skills` is loaded by Reasonix at runtime but invisible to the Library's accounting for it — "which agents have this skill" would leave Reasonix out while it reads the folder. On this machine that is 10 skills under `~/.agents/skills` beside 22 under `%APPDATA%\reasonix\skills`.

Suggested fix: add `"reasonix"` to `readsShared`. `.agent` can stay uncovered — no magpie target uses it either.

The same is true one level down: `projectSkillsDirs["reasonix"] = ".reasonix/skills"` covers one of the four convention dirs a project gets. That may be deliberate (magpie's project table also lists a single dir per agent), so I'd only flag it, not ask for it.

## Verification offer

I have Studio 2.50.0 and magpie 0.1.1364 here on Windows, and `%APPDATA%\reasonix\` is a real install rather than a sandbox. Say which commit to build and I'll run the Library sync against it and report what it writes.

@FuchaZ Thanks for the Studio 2.50.0 source pointers and for offering a real Windows check. I have implemented the remaining Reasonix Library integration directly, in a **standalone branch** rather than the mixed round-10 batch:

https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/reasonix-library-complete-1024
head: `cf87dc37c09e5b6fbadebfd7ebc8adcd9f102290`

This branch is based on upstream `dd1e8822` and contains the #3401 MCP/skills baseline plus:
- Hooks in Reasonix's **own** `<Reasonix home>/settings.json`, `hooks.<Event>[]` flat entries (not Claude's nested form).
- Portable and Reasonix-native event names from `internal/ext/hook/hook.go`. Tool matchers use anchored regex against the actual native tool names (`bash`, `edit_file`, `write_file`, `multi_edit`); `timeout` is stored in **milliseconds**.
- Skill accounting for `~/.agents/skills` via `readsShared`, in addition to Reasonix's own and Claude's skill folders.
- Round-trip and ownership checks: write, read, remove only Magpie-managed entries, preserve the user's existing hooks, settings and MCP array tables.

`go test -tags nogui ./internal/library -count=1` passes on this branch; Linux and Windows/amd64 static vet passed. **I have not run Reasonix natively on Windows**, so please do not treat this as a native end-to-end check.

If you can build this exact head against your Reasonix Studio 2.50.0 installation, please verify that Library-created hooks actually fire for `bash` and `edit_file/write_file`, that existing `settings.json` entries remain untouched when a Library hook is removed, and that shared skills under `~/.agents/skills` are correctly reported. A redacted before/after config and the first event's result would be valuable. Thanks again for the precise schema details.

This is a fork contribution offered for review, not a claim that upstream has accepted it.

timeline.body:
Ran it. Built `cf87dc37` with Go 1.26.8 (portable, nothing installed) and exercised it against a **real Windows install**, not a sandbox: Reasonix Studio **2.50.0** (`reasonix-studio-electron`, read from `resources/app.asar`) with magpie 0.1.1391 on Windows 11. All three things you asked for are below.

## 1. Library-created hooks do fire, for `bash`

Wrote a `UserPromptSubmit` hook through `magpie library sync`, then drove a turn with the Studio CLI's own non-interactive mode (`reasonix -p --permission-mode danger-full-access`). The hook ran:

```
PRE  2026/10/24 23:03:09.28
POST 2026/10/24 23:03:09.54
```

Those two lines are the `PreToolUse` / `PostToolUse` probes I had in `settings.json` firing around an actual `bash` call in the turn, so `match: "^(bash|edit_file|write_file|multi_edit)$"` matches the **native** Reasonix tool name, exactly as you wrote it. The turn itself ran `echo HOOK_E2E_TEST_12345` and returned it.

One thing worth recording for upstream: Studio reports the file as loaded, so you can check a machine without running a turn.

```
$ reasonix hook list --json
{"hooks":[{"event":"PostToolUse","match":"^(bash|edit_file|write_file|multi_edit)$","scope":"global","status":"active"},
          {"event":"PreToolUse","match":"^(bash|edit_file|write_file|multi_edit)$","scope":"global","status":"active"}]}
```

## 2. Existing entries survive, in both directions

Put a user-owned entry in the file first:

```json
"Stop": [{ "command": "...", "description": "USER-OWNED-HOOK" }]
```

Then `magpie library sync` with a Library hook ticked for reasonix. Both ended up in the file, the user's untouched:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "UserPromptSubmit": [ { "command": "..." } ],   <- magpie's
    "PreToolUse":  [ { "match": "...", "command": "..." } ],
    "PostToolUse": [ { "match": "...", "command": "..." } ],
    "Stop": [ { "command": "...", "description": "USER-OWNED-HOOK" } ]   <- the user's, verbatim
  }
}
```

Then removed the Library hook and synced again. `UserPromptSubmit` went, `Stop` stayed byte-identical, with its `description` intact.

Same for MCP, on the array-table side: added a server with `library mcp add … agents=reasonix`, confirmed `name = 'probe-x'` landed in `config.toml` beside the user's own six `[[plugins]]`, removed it, and the six were unchanged and the probe gone. `[[providers]]` and the rest of the file were never touched.

## 3. `~/.agents/skills` accounting

`reasonix` is in `readsShared`, and `TestReasonixSharedSkillsAccounting` passes here — a skill present in `~/.agents/skills` is now reported as one reasonix has, instead of silently being read at runtime while the Library says it doesn't have it.

Your own test file covers it; I did not construct a separate end-to-end fixture for this one, since the unit test asserts exactly the `Always` membership the page reads.

## Test evidence

```
$ go test -tags nogui ./internal/library -run 'Reasonix' -count=1 -v
--- PASS: TestReasonixHooksOwnShapeAndPreservation (0.08s)
--- PASS: TestReasonixSharedSkillsAccounting (0.04s)
--- PASS: TestReasonixPluginsMCP (0.06s)
PASS
ok  github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/library  0.270s
```

**Caveats, stated plainly:**

- I exercised hooks through the **Studio CLI** (`reasonix -p`), which shares `<Reasonix home>/settings.json` with the desktop app but is not the Electron window. Same loader, same file, same 2.50.0 build — but if you want the GUI path specifically, that is still untested.
- My probe hooks were removed and both files restored to their exact prior contents afterwards; `settings.json` is back to `{"hooks": {}}` and `config.toml` still has its original six `[[plugins]]`. No before/after diff of a *user-owned* MCP or hook is included because I would rather not publish your config — the shape above is the redacted version.
- Everything ran on this machine's real `%APPDATA%\reasonix`, with magpie's own backups taken at each sync (`~/.config/magpie/backups/…`), so each step is reversible.

Two small observations while I was in there, neither blocking:

- `library sync` reports `✓ written into reasonix` even when only hooks changed, which reads a little oddly when the log above it says MCP servers were untouched.
- The hook row's `match` is stored as `^(bash|edit_file|write_file|multi_edit)$`. Reasonix anchors it again itself (`^(?:` + m + `)$`), so it's harmless, but `^…$` in the stored value double-anchors.

Nice work on the flat `match`/`command`/`timeout` shape — it lines up with the 2.50.0 source exactly, and the round-trip preserved the user's entry with its `description` intact without any special-casing.

这份验证已记录在案，round-13 留的"真实 Windows Studio 2.50.0 上验证 hook 触发与共享技能识别"这一项就此关闭：`PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` 探针在真实 `bash` 调用前后触发（原生工具名匹配生效）、用户自有的 `Stop` 条目与六个 `[[plugins]]` 在双向同步后逐字节保留、`~/.agents/skills` 经 `readsShared` 计入。`hook list --json` 能离线确认装载，这条对上游也有用，记下了。GUI（Electron 窗口）路径仍未测，与你的 caveat 一致——CLI 与桌面共用同一 loader 和 settings.json，风险很小，但不算已验证。

两个观察都收到，都同意不阻塞，说明一下我们的取舍：

- **match 双重锚定**：同意是无操作——Reasonix 包一层 `^(?:…)$` 后，`^(?:^X$)$` 与 `^X$` 匹配的串完全相同。锚定形态是 magpie 的规范条目形状：同步记录按它做认领与移除（`internal/library/hooks.go` 的 records 比对），且正是这份在真机上验证过触发行为的形状。改成不锚定需要重新走一遍真机验证才能声称有效，收益只是文件里少四个字符，所以暂时保留；如果上游愿意收，随收随改。
- **"✓ written into reasonix"**：`Changed` 的语义是"哪些 agent 的文件被写过"，即使只动了 hooks 一节，settings.json 确实重写了。让它按节报变化需要重构 Result 的粒度，为此一项只影响观感的输出不值得，保留原样。

两处都已记入本 fork 的 ledger 与 evidence（[comment 6385801640](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3401#issuecomment-6385801640)，你的测试输出与保留意见一并）。你环境里probe 的清理与备份说明也已记录。

## 摘要（给扫 issue 的人看）

**问题**：Reasonix Studio 在 magpie 里只接了模型（executor/planner/effort），Library 层的 MCP、skills、hooks 全都没有。结果是：在 Library 页面里配好 MCP 和技能，勾选不到 Reasonix Studio。

**现状**：**实现已经写好了，只差维护者收割。**

- 代码：`skygunner/magpie` 分支 `fix/reasonix-library-complete-1024`，head `cf87dc37`
- 覆盖：MCP（`[[plugins]]`）、skills（含 `~/.agents/skills`）、hooks（`.reasonix/settings.json`）三项齐全
- 验证：**已在真实 Windows 上跑通** —— Reasonix Studio 2.50.0 + magpie 0.1.1391，`PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse` 在真实 `bash` 调用前后触发，用户自有 hook 与 6 个 `[[plugins]]` 双向同步逐字节保留

以上细节都在本 issue 前面的评论里（含 Studio 源码里的 hooks schema、字段差异、真机测试输出）。

**不需要再讨论设计了，只差有人把它并进 main。** 这个仓库现在不收外部 PR，所以只能等维护者看到这条。

---

## 中文补充：为什么我在意这个

我用 Reasonix Studio（2.50.0）作为主力 agent，同时也用 magpie 统一管理模型。

现在的情况有点尴尬：

- 模型能选 magpie 的 ✅
- 但 Library 里配的 MCP、技能、hooks 给不了它 ❌

更麻烦的是它**看起来像能用**：Studio 里确实能看到 context7、deepwiki 这些 MCP，但那是 Reasonix 自己去读 `~/.claude.json` 蹭来的，不是 magpie 配的。所以在 magpie 里「按 Agent 启用 MCP」这个动作，对它完全无效——勾不上，也没提示为什么。

期待的行为很简单：

| 功能 | 期望 |
| --- | --- |
| MCP 服务器 | 能勾选 Reasonix Studio，写进 `config.toml` 的 `[[plugins]]` |
| Skills | 能勾选，写进 `<reasonix home>/skills`，并识别 `~/.agents/skills` |
| Hooks | 能勾选，写进 `.reasonix/settings.json` |

不用改模型那条链路，那部分（#427）一直好好的。

感谢。
